description:
1. Monthly Fire Suppression Inspections   PWS Sections 5, 6.1, and Appendix B
The revised PWS shows Section 6.1 (Monthly Inspections) and the corresponding monthly inspection requirement in Appendix B as struck through. However, Sections 1 and 5 and Appendix A still reference monthly inspections.
Could the Government please confirm whether the requirement for monthly inspections of all 10 fire suppression systems (120 inspections annually) has been officially removed, leaving only the semiannual maintenance and certification requirements?
Leaving these references in was an error. All references to monthly inspections should be disregarded, as they are no longer required. 

2. Monthly Reconciliation and Deficiency Log   PWS Section 10 and Appendix B
The revised Appendix B shows the monthly reconciliation and deficiency log deliverable as struck through, while Section 10 continues to require monthly reconciliation by the fifth business day of the following month.
Could the Government confirm whether monthly reconciliation reports are still required, or whether this reporting obligation has been removed? We understand that service-specific deficiency reporting remains applicable.
Section 10 is not referencing monthly inspections. It is references service reports. Since work is not being done monthly, the language should be revised to say, Â  With each service report, the Contractor shall update the cumulative equipment inventory, service log, and deficiency log. Identify required services that were not completed, the reasons, and proposed completion dates. Update open deficiencies when corrective work is completed. A combined visit may satisfy multiple required activities only when each activity and its results are separately documented. A separate monthly reconciliation report is not required. 


3. Existing Deficiencies and Six-Year Cylinder Maintenance   PWS Section 9
The historical kitchen exhaust cleaning reports identify inaccessible duct sections, recommended access-panel installations, and other conditions requiring corrective action.
Additionally, the October 2026 fire suppression inspection records identify six-year maintenance concerns affecting the Kidde dry-chemical systems, while the November 2026 maintenance documentation appears to address four cylinders.
Could the Government please clarify:
Whether the identified duct-access deficiencies will be corrected before the new contract begins or addressed separately through Contracting Officer-authorized corrective work.
Whether the six-year maintenance requirements have been fully completed for all five Kidde IND-21 systems, or whether any outstanding work remains.
Whether any unresolved pre-existing deficiencies should be excluded from recurring fixed-price services and handled through separate authorization under Section 9.
The Six-Year maintenance deficiency was corrected on November 19th, 2026. The VA is not aware of any duct-access deficiencies, this was not listed in the previous report to the one you referenced and may be an administrative error. Offeror should make their own assessment during a scheduled site visit.
